slide.text: Housing delivery, land formalisation, extractives governance, and agency coordination all depend on faster and more trusted workflows.

text.p: Nigeria’s biggest delivery bottlenecks are rarely caused by lack of demand alone. They are caused by fragmented records, disconnected approvals, weak evidence continuity, and slow coordination between field teams and decision desks.

For federal institutions, this creates weak oversight across land, housing, mining, oil and gas, and infrastructure-linked approvals. For states and builders, it translates into slower project starts, uncertain compliance status, weaker revenue visibility, and lower citizen confidence.

p.strong: The platform matters because it connects approvals to place, evidence, deadlines, and accountability in one operating model.

tr.td: Approval delays directly affect housing supply, affordability, project mobilisation, and the pace at which formal developments can move to market.[1]

td.strong: Land formalisation remains below 10%, with ambition to reach 50% in 10 years

tr.td: Weak records limit mortgage depth, investor confidence, land-based revenue, and the efficiency of state land administration.[1]

td.strong: The mining cadastre already manages 5,000+ mineral titles and 2,000+ applications annually

tr.td: High-volume approvals require transparent workflow, stronger evidence handling, and clearer coordination across technical and regulatory review functions.[2]

slide.text: This is why the platform is positioned as delivery infrastructure for Nigeria, not just software for forms.
